college_identity.verified_name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar
college_identity.identity_notes: Formerly Regional Engineering College (REC), Jalandhar, established 1987 (some sources cite 1989) as a joint venture of the Government of India and Government of Punjab; upgraded to NIT/Deemed University status on 17 October 2002; declared Institute of National Importance in 2004/2007 (sources vary on exact year). No conflicting institutions of similar name identified; one search result referenced 'DAV College' and 'Lovely Professional University' as separate, unrelated nearby institutions in the same city, correctly not conflated with NIT Jalandhar.

review_items.review_title: Which one is better for CSE. USICT or NIT Jalandhar? What are the pros and cons of each?
review_items.extraction_note: This is an unusually detailed, structured pros-and-cons answer covering multiple aspects with specific named details, split into multiple aspect_evidence entries below.

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'Jalandhar City - The city is itself a students hub. Various other institutes like DAV College, Lovely Professional University, CT College are also situated in Jalandhar. Also the city has all the amenities of a big city but is not overcrowded like Ludhiana or Amritsar... NITJ has an advantage geographically. It is very close to many hill stations and places you can go on during short vacations like Manali, Dharamsala, Rishikesh, Vaishno Devi, Chandigarh, Rohtang etc.'

'Cultural & Technical Fest - Utkarsh & Techniti, the cultural & technical fests of NITJ attract colleges from the whole of North India. You get a lot of opportunity to participate in various fun & technical activities during these fests.'

'Placements - The placements at NITJ are comparatively good for most of the branches. CS had the best placements followed by mechanical and even textile technology. So even if you are an average student you can get decent enough placement.'
'No ragging - There is almost no ragging at NITJ. There is separate hostel for 1st year students to stop ragging.'

'Hostel Timing restrictions - One of the worse things I felt at NITJ was restrictive hostel timings. It was up to 10 pm during my time but now it has been raised to 12 midnight for both boys and girls.'

'1st year restrictions - Because of separate hostel for 1st year students, there were many restrictions also. Hostel timings would not be the same as the whole campus. Also, there is no LAN connection in Hostel-1 (during our time it was not there). 1st year students stay in either Hostel-1 or Hostel-2; comparatively H-2 is better in terms of timings and LAN.'

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'There are 7 standing alone hostels plus Mega Hostels Block A, B, E, F. Standing Alone hostels are numbered as 1-7 and 7E. Hostel 1 & 2 are entirely for first year undergrads. No, freshers will not get a single room unless medically or [via] special allotment.'
